title: Propellant load begins
description: Super Heavy and Starship begin loading liquid methane and liquid oxygen.

title: Raptor engine chill
description: Cryogenic propellant flows through the Raptors to condition them for ignition.

title: Flight director verifies GO for launch
Water deluge activates
description: The steel flame deflector sprays water to absorb the acoustic and thermal energy of 33 Raptors.

title: Liftoff
description: Super Heavy B21 and Ship 41 lift off from Orbital Launch Pad 2 at Starbase, Texas.

title: Max Q
description: Moment of peak mechanical stress on the rocket.

title: Booster engine shutdown
description: One Super Heavy Raptor shuts down early, about a minute into flight. The remaining 32 engines compensate.

title: Booster MECO
description: Most Super Heavy engines cut off (main engine cutoff).

title: Hot staging
description: Starship lights all six engines while still attached and pushes away from Super Heavy through the vented hot-stage ring.

title: Booster boostback burn start
description: 31 of the 33 planned engines relight. The burn deliberately runs the main LOX tank dry to probe performance limits.

title: Booster landing burn start
description: 11 of 13 planned engines relight, then the booster steps down to 5, then 3 engines.

title: Booster landing burn steps down to 5, then 3 engines
Booster landing burn shutdown and splashdown
description: Super Heavy B21 makes a soft, controlled splashdown in the Gulf a few miles off the Texas coast.

title: Booster flight termination demo
description: After shutdown, B21's flight termination system fires as a planned demonstration of the safety hardware.

title: Ship Raptor Vacuum engine out
description: One of Ship 41's three Raptor Vacuum engines shuts down early. The other five engines burn longer to reach the planned trajectory.

title: Ship engine cutoff (SECO)
description: Ship engine cutoff comes later than planned (~8:11) because of the longer burn on five engines.

title: “Not going to commit to orbit”
description: After the RVac shutdown the team first decides to stay suborbital, with no Starlink deploy and an Indian Ocean splashdown.

title: GO for orbit
description: After a poll lasting about 20 minutes, flight director's call: “We are go for orbit.” The Starbase crowd erupts.

title: Orbital insertion burn start
description: A single sea-level Raptor relights, fed for the first time from the header tanks.

title: Orbital insertion burn shutdown
description: Starship is in orbit for the first time: about 262 × 275 km at 30.5°.

title: PEZ door opens
description: The payload bay camera shows the Starlink dispenser door opening, starting the deploy sequence.

title: Starlink deployment begins
description: The first Starlink V3 satellite slides out of the PEZ dispenser slot. Three carry cameras to image Ship 41's heat shield.

title: Starlink deployment complete
description: All 26 Starlink V3 satellites released. SpaceX contacts them through laser links, ground stations and user terminals.

title: Early deorbit decision
description: SpaceX shortens the planned six-orbit, 10-hour mission and targets the northern Pacific, one of two pre-cleared zones.

title: Live HD video from orbit via Starlink
description: For the first time, live views of Starship in orbit are relayed through Starlink laser links.

title: Deorbit burn start
description: First-ever Starship deorbit burn, on one sea-level Raptor, targeting the northern Pacific contingency zone.

title: Ship entry
description: Entry interface. Plasma builds around the heat shield, which includes two reflown tiles from Ship 40.

title: Ship landing burn start
description: All three sea-level Raptors relight.

title: Ship splashdown
description: Ship 41 splashes down several hundred kilometres north of Hawaii. A buoy camera captures it tipping over and exploding about six seconds later.

title: Ship tips over and residual propellant ignites
